title: Unresolved radiation (mock)
goal: Mock dataset (not empirical or user data). Distinguish an unresolved five-way split from the resolved D/E sister pair.

rubric.must: A, B, C, the D/E ancestor, and F meet at one root without invented binary ancestors.
D and E share a separate ancestor.
All six tips and their individual branches remain distinguishable.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the phylo/slanted exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing visibly matches the authored phylogram: Reef A, B, C, the D/E ancestral branch, and Reef F emerge from one root; Reef D and E then split at their own shared ancestor. All six tips and branches are clearly distinguishable.

items.evidence: Five lineages visibly meet at the single left root: Reef A, Reef B, Reef C, the branch leading to the D/E ancestor, and Reef F. No extra binary ancestors are shown.
Reef D and Reef E visibly diverge from a separate shared node downstream of the root and are also identified by the D/E sister-pair bracket.
All six labeled tips—Reef A through Reef F—are legible, and each has a distinct visible terminal branch.
